title: Scam or OK?

items.text: Text (unknown number): Your parcel is waiting for a customs payment of €1.29. Without payment it will be returned today. Pay here: parcel-payment.example
items.why: It aims at hurry (“today”) and a small amount that doesn't look suspicious.

items.text: E-mail (Class teacher · school address): Hello, on Friday we're going on a school trip. Meet at 8:00 in front of the school, bring a snack and a drink. You'll find the details in the school system.
items.why: It doesn't want anything: no link, no details, no hurry.

items.text: E-mail (Game team): Congratulations! You've won 2,000 gems in the contest. Collect your prize within 24 hours by logging in with your game account: game-rewards.example
items.why: It aims at reward and hurry. The text doesn't have a single mistake. AI wrote it.

items.text: Call (Mum · unknown number): “Hi, it's me. My phone broke, I'm calling from someone else's. You'll get a text with a code, read it out to me, quickly. I'll explain at home.”
items.why: It aims at trust and fear for someone close. The voice may be cloned by AI.

items.text: Text (Game): (You are logging in to the game right now.) Login code: 482913. Don't give it to anyone, not even support.
items.why: The code came because you are the one logging in right now. It belongs only in the login window.

items.text: Chat (Your friend Tomáš): Hey, please vote for me in a contest! Just log in with your account here: contest-vote.example 🙏
items.why: It aims at friendship. Tomáš's account may already be controlled by a scammer.

debrief: You can spot a scam by hurry, an unfamiliar link and a request for a code, a password or a payment. When you're not sure, check it another way: in the app, with a teacher or on a number you know.
